ai.purpose: RTT/3 engine layer for Information Theory: triadic-substrate integration, multi-regime simulation hooks, distinction-resonance mapping, and hybrid-canon scaffolding.

engine.description: Integrates Information Theory into the triadic substrate, enabling multi-regime reasoning, distinction propagation, and hybrid-canon simulation.

mapping.structure: Distinctions map to substrate state separations; entropy reflects distribution over these separations.
mapping.behavior: Information flow emerges from resonance alignment between constraints and channel structure.
mapping.capacity: Channel capacity corresponds to stable resonance bandwidth under substrate invariants.

constraints: Propagation speed and bandwidth are substrate invariants.

R0.behavior: Pure distinctions; information defined without physical substrate.
R0.notes: Entropy and codes exist as abstract operators.

R1.behavior: Primitive channels; minimal carriers and noise.

R2.behavior: Physical, biological, or computational implementations of codes and channels.

R3.behavior: Complex multi-channel systems with robust error correction and redundancy.

hooks.description: Models entropy gradients as resonance flows between uncertainty and constraint.

hooks.name: code_stability_sim

simulation.notes: Simulations operate on distinctions, constraints, and resonance patterns, not on physical substrates unless specified.

hybrid_canon.purpose: Enable agentic AIs to reason across physics, biology, and computation using shared informational invariants.
